checks.evidence: Action: Observe the rendered sun and three moving planets, select each, measure orbital readouts over 3.10-second intervals, and seek 0/17/30/73/120. Expected: distinct spheres on fixed circular 12/24/48-second orbits. Observed: one gold sun and orange small Aurelia, cyan medium Pelagos, lavender larger Nivalis; changing perspective showed spheres on circular orbital paths. Fixed phases were 15/145/260 degrees. At 1x Aurelia moved 171.26 to 264.44 degrees as time 17.21 to 20.31 in 3.103 wall seconds; Pelagos 43.33 to 89.75 as 17.22 to 20.32 in 3.108; Nivalis 29.09 to 52.39 as 17.21 to 20.32 in 3.107. These agree with 30/15/7.5 degrees per simulation second within preregistered precision. Predicted projected planet locations also accepted actual scene clicks.

Action: Load fresh fixtures and reload after persistence operations. Expected: time-zero initialization, running at 1x, null selection, overview, subsequent motion. Observed: reload samples at 0.04, 0.05 and 0.06 seconds showed 1x, Pause playback, no selected planet and Full-system overview; later readouts and rendered positions advanced. The tiny elapsed startup times are loading delay, not evidence of nonzero initialization. Tracking was disabled and no highlight was present.

Action: Pause motion, seek, wait 3.1 seconds, select/orbit while paused, then resume. Expected: frozen time/positions and continuous restart. Observed: time 73 remained 73 with byte-identical full rendered screenshots after 3.1 seconds. Paused planet selection and orbit/zoom worked. Resume from 30 at 2x began at 30.42 and reached 36.82 over 3.203 seconds, with no reset or observed positional jump.

Action: Set 0.25x, 2x and 4x paused at 17, resume and measure each, and change between those speeds while playing. Expected: preserved current position/time, proportional rates, no resume jump. Observed: paused samples remained 17 at all three speeds. Measured deltas were 0.80 in 3.211 wall seconds at 0.25x, 6.40 in 3.203 at 2x, and 12.80 in 3.203 at 4x, with visible document and only this review scene running. Playing speed changes preserved the sampled time to display precision (17.86 to 17.86, 23.82 to 23.84, 30.64 to 30.64); a separate 1x-to-2x change was 17.21 to 17.21 and remained playing. Relative orbit rates and positions agreed with the fixed-period angle checks.

Action: Seek 0/17/30/73/120, change speed/playback/selection, repeat 30/17/73, and reload then seek 73 again. Expected: immediate paused, deterministic positions and information. Observed: all seeks paused. Aurelia/Pelagos/Nivalis angles were respectively 15/145/260 at 0, 165/40/27.5 at 17, 195/235/125 at 30, 45/160/87.5 at 73, and 15/145/80 at 120. Repeated same-framing screenshots at 30/17/73 were byte-identical; the 73-second screenshot after reload also matched exactly. Imported time 17.25 restored angles 172.50/43.75/29.38, not supplied fake angles.

Action: Seek 119, play at 4x across the endpoint, wait again, seek 17 and resume. Expected: stop exactly at 120 without wrapping and allow earlier playback. Observed: 120 with Resume playback after 1.1 seconds and still 120 after an additional wait; subsequent 17-second seek/resume advanced to 19.28 at 4x.

Action: Inspect local renderer/geometry dependency and actual HTTP resources, then orbit and zoom the scene in both modes. Expected: genuine Three.js 3D rendering. Observed: output/index.html loads local three.min.js and constructs WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera, SphereGeometry, torus highlights and circular line geometry (lines 83-92). Browser resource timing recorded the local three.min.js request and the scene-error display stayed empty. Transient rendered images showed shaded spheres, front/back overlap of highlight rings, changing orbit-plane perspective and changing apparent sphere size under orbit/zoom, not a flat drawing.

Observed: paused capture aba97eb1-5880-4e03-9051-96b5793654d3 retained 30 seconds, 2x, Aurelia, tracking and 195/235/125 degrees after live edits and playback. Playing capture 348709d0-4984-4b32-b2a1-4d84bf68494f at 0.107 seconds retained its ID, fields and 18.20/146.60/260.80 angles across reload. Capture preserved live playback and selection. Action: Select every planet through both canvas and directory while paused and playing. Expected: one shared selection, visible highlight and matching information. Observed: actual canvas clicks selected Aurelia/Pelagos/Nivalis at paused time 17 with angles 165/40/27.50 and again during 0.25x playback with corresponding evolving angles. Directory clicks and keyboard activation selected all three. Gold rings and pressed directory buttons followed the selected sphere, including paused states.

Action: Inspect all selected names, periods and live angles during playback and seeks, then restore a null-selection record after tracking. Restoring null overview displayed No planet selected, removed highlight and disabled tracking, rather than retaining previous planet details.

Action: Track moving Nivalis over more than three seconds, seek to 30 and 73, switch all planet selections while paused and switch to Aurelia while playing; inspect initial null-selection tracking control. Expected: synchronized target/highlight/info centered without changing unrelated state; null tracking unavailable. Observed: mobile scene was approximately 343x355 CSS pixels; the tracked sphere remained at its scene center, within roughly 2 CSS pixels versus the 34.3-pixel tolerance, across 30-second pause, playback from about 31 to 44.29 over 3.365 wall seconds, and seek 73. Paused switches at 17 retained 1.5x and pause while each sphere centered. Playing switch retained 1.5x and running, advancing naturally to 17.74. Null-selection startup/restores disabled Track planet.

Action: At 390x844 select Nivalis, seek 30, enable tracking, then press Full overview. Expected: full system visible with unchanged time/speed/selection/playback. Observed: state remained 30, 4x, Nivalis, paused, but most of Nivalis was cut off by the left canvas boundary; the outer orbit also extended outside the scene. Desktop overview was fully visible. This violates full-system framing, not state preservation. Source support: standardFraming uses distance 32 irrespective of aspect ratio (line 59), while resize changes only camera aspect (line 91).

Action: Import null overview at time 30/speed 1.5 and selected tracking at 17.25, restore after unrelated live edits and manual orbit/zoom, repeat at the same viewport, then restore the null record at 390x844. Expected: atomic paused state and deterministic standard full-system or selected-planet framing. Observed: restored fields, positions, target and cleared information were correct; repeated desktop tracking and overview screenshots matched exactly once scroll framing matched. However mobile null-overview restore at 30 clipped most of Nivalis at the left canvas boundary, so its standard overview is not full-system framing. The same fixed-distance camera cause as T4 affects this separate restore requirement.

Action: Drag and wheel-zoom in overview/tracking both paused and playing. Expected: actual camera orbit and zoom around current target without simulation mutation. Paused examples stayed time 17, 4x, Nivalis selected; playing examples advanced naturally to 18.43 while mode and selection remained unchanged. Tracking kept its selected sphere centered as the background geometry changed.

Action: Reload after valid import, deletion and capture; replace only the app storage key with malformed and schema-invalid data; exhaust bounded origin quota using one reviewer filler key and capture through UI. Expected: persistent validated list with default live state, visible recovery/saving-unavailable feedback, usable memory state. Malformed JSON and time 121 persisted payloads each produced empty list and Saved observations could not be recovered notice; selection and playback remained usable. Filler accepted 5,242,553 characters within the fixed 8 MiB bound. Capture then created an in-memory entry while the persisted empty payload stayed unchanged and Saving unavailable...unsaved changes may not survive reload appeared, establishing an actual failed app write. Selection/playback continued. Filler was removed, exact fixture-original app value restored, and both cleanup predicates were true. This is quota-write recovery, not storage-read-denial testing.
